findings.claim: The static-vs-dynamic import guard uses single-line anchored regexes (/^import .* from "ai";/m, /^import .*activeAiModel/m), so a multi-line static import — the exact shape the repo's formatting produces for a longer import list — would not be caught while the positive import("ai") assertions still pass.
findings.reproduction: In lib/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter.ts add `import {\n    generateText,\n} from "ai";` at the top while leaving `import("ai")` in runPromptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter, then run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`: all four assertions at :269-272 still pass even though the provider SDK now loads at module load. Matching /from\s+"ai"/ (or `@\/lib\/activeAiModel"`) outside a dynamic-import context instead closes this.

findings.claim: The repo-wide unreachability scan only matches /\.(?:ts|tsx|mjs)$/ files, so a future .js/.cjs/.jsx entry point, or a package.json script pointing node directly at the adapter, would not be caught by the guard that is this change's primary safety mechanism.
findings.reproduction: Add `scripts/run-refiner.cjs` containing `require("../lib/promptRefinerShadowLiveAdapter")` and run `npm run test:prompt-refiner-shadow-live-adapter`: the "no shipped entry point imports the live adapter" test still passes. I confirmed no .js/.cjs/.jsx/.mts files exist today under app, lib, scripts, components, hooks, prisma or .railway, so this is latent rather than current.
